claims.claim_text: As we step into 2025, we remain committed to driving sustainable growth, leveraging our resilience and focus on innovation to create long-term value.
Indorama Ventures delivered an improved financial performance in 2024, demonstrating resilience and a commitment to decisive management actions under our IVL 2.0 transformation strategy.
Our disciplined execution led to an adjusted EBITDA of $1.52 billion, marking a 9.7% increase from the previous year, and a strong production volume of 14.04 million tons with a 79% operating rate.

Guided by our IVL 2.0 strategy, we are securing our future as a company that generates sustainable and growing shareholder returns, with a focus on organic growth, financial discipline, developing future-ready leaders, and leading the transition to a low-carbon economy.
The acquisitions of intellectual properties include pioneering solutions such as KEMELIX and FLOWSOLVE that accelerate our presence in energy extraction markets.
Our commitment to ESG-focused investments and sustainable finance ensures that every step we take aligns with our broader environmental and social objectives.

Securing a $200 million, seven-year loan from the International Finance Corporation (IFC) will accelerate sustainability initiatives in India, Thailand, and Indonesia, as well as fuel our circular economy ambitions and reinforce our position as the global leader in PET recycling.
Our investments in bio-PET and sustainable fibers continue to set new benchmarks in circularity and carbon reduction, with bio-PET production in 2024 totaling about 28,000 tons.

In collaboration with Suntory, ENEOS Corporation, Mitsubishi Corporation, Iwatani, and Neste, we launched the world’s first commercialized bio-PET bottle using ISCC+ certified bio-paraxylene, reducing fossil dependency and CO₂ emissions.
We sold about 8,000 tons of bio-PET resin to Suntory in 2024, and we expect a similar offtake in 2025.

We have joined a consortium of seven companies across five countries to establish a supply chain for more sustainable polyester fiber, produced from renewable and bio-based raw materials, including paraxylene from carbon capture and utilization.
Despite progress in our Environmental, Health & Safety targets, we recorded a number of accidents in 2024, including four that resulted in fatalities.

By investing in advanced recycling and low-carbon technologies, and expanding our global recycling facilities footprint, we continue to set new benchmarks in sustainability while reinforcing our commitment to a more sustainable future.

We integrated climate adaptation into our sustainability strategy using a three-phase approach - Readiness & Capacity Building (2024-2025), Planning (2026), and Implementation (2027) - to maintain resilience against climate risks.
We established in-house Life Cycle Management expertise and performed product Life Cycle Assessments to facilitate our customers’ needs.
The overall GHG scope 1&2 intensity reduction at the end of 2024 is projected to be 1.09%, with an anticipated reduction of 1.14% by 2025, against a target of a 10% reduction from the 2020 baseline.
Since 2011, our commitment to recycling has resulted in establishing 852,000 tons of bale input capacity.

In 2024 alone, over 396,000 tons of post-consumer PET bottles (equivalent to more than 26 billion bottles) were recycled, further solidifying our leadership in the PET circular economy and driving industry-wide transformation.
From 2011-2024, we recycled more than 135 billion PET bottles, diverting 2.6 million tons of plastic waste from landfills and preventing 3.6 million tons of CO₂ emissions by 2024.

As sustainability regulations and standards—such as the EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), the EU Taxonomy, and IFRS Standards—reshape global markets, we are proactively aligning our business practices to enhance investor confidence, unlock sustainable financing opportunities, and future-proof our operations.
Our focus on ESG transparency, resource efficiency, and regulatory compliance strengthens our financial resilience while delivering long-term value to all stakeholders.

In 2024, Indorama Ventures remained focused on strengthening its financial foundation, reinforcing financial discipline, and pursuing a forward-looking investment strategy aligned with our transformation roadmap.
As part of our evolving financial strategy, we are integrating ESG-aligned performance indicators into executive accountability and capital allocation frameworks.
We continuously track and disclose greenhouse gas emissions intensity relative to revenue, offering a clearer picture of carbon productivity.

Talent development remained a priority in 2024, with targeted initiatives in inclusive recruitment, global internship programs, and academic partnerships to attract and grow future talents.

At Indorama Ventures, employee well-being is a key driver of organizational resilience, performance, and long-term sustainability.
In 2024, we continued to advance our Corporate Well-being Reinvention Framework, emphasizing flexibility, inclusion, and personal fulfillment at work.

At Indorama Ventures, we uphold the rights and dignity of all individuals. Our commitment is rooted in internationally recognized human rights frameworks, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR), the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs), UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989) and the International Labour Organization (ILO)’s Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work.

We are committed to “Protect, Respect, and Remedy” framework and proactively identifying, addressing, and preventing human rights risks across our operations, while ensuring full compliance with applicable local and international laws.
Our Human Rights Policy and Responsible Sourcing Policy extend these expectations to suppliers, subcontractors, and vendors.
We are committed to maintaining transparency across our operations and throughout our supply chain in the fight against modern slavery.
In 2023, it was expanded to explicitly address modern slavery and human trafficking.
As of 2024, no incidents related to modern slavery have been reported.
Indorama Ventures’ Human Rights Due Diligence (HRDD) framework is embedded across our operations, supply chains, and the communities we touch.
In 2024, we conducted risk assessments across all operational sites, focusing on health and safety, child labor, discrimination, and working conditions.
We achieved a 100% declaration rate, with no significant violations reported.
Six human rights-related issues were identified in 2024, marking a reduction from the previous year.
Our Responsible Sourcing Policy clearly sets expectations for suppliers regarding ethical conduct, labor rights, health and safety, and environmental stewardship.
100% human rights risk assessments across all manufacturing locations
100% human rights declarations signed by business heads and site heads
No significant human rights issues or major violations recorded in our operations or supply chain
Approximately 900 employees participated in 30 onsite and online Human Rights Policy training sessions.
Strengthened employee data security and privacy protection in compliance with Thailand’s PDPA (2012) and the EU GDPR
80% of raw material suppliers were assessed based on human rights-related risks
No suppliers were identified as being exposed to risks of incidents of child, forced, and compulsory labor
We are committed to embedding ESG safeguards throughout our operations and broader business network.

The 2024 Sustainability Report reflects the ongoing dedication of Indorama Ventures to adhering to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) standards while outlining our comprehensive strategy for generating value that considers both tangible and intangible, as well as financial and non-financial aspects of the business.

In alignment with the 2021 Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards, International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) S1 and S2, and the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), we detail our sustainability initiatives and their links to our financial performance, assessing our position as a sustainable chemical company within the reporting scope.

We have implemented robust internal controls and verification processes to uphold data accuracy and reliability while reaffirming our unwavering commitment to ethical business conduct, responsible decision-making, and long-term value creation for all of our stakeholders.

We are expanding the scope of our reporting to further improve transparency and align with global best practices by integrating double materiality, capturing both financial and impact-driven material concerns.
Our approach adopts an integrated reporting framework in line with GRI, IFRS S1 and S2, and CSRD, providing a holistic view of our sustainability performance.
Additionally, our reporting incorporates insights from the UN Global Compact (UNGC), the 56-1 One Report, and the AA1000 Assurance Standard to enhance regional and global relevance.

To ensure broader accountability, we are aligning our disclosures with leading sustainability benchmarks including the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP), Dow Jones Sustainability Indices (DJSI), Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI), and Sustainalytics.
In 2024, we expanded our data verification coverage from 149 to 150 operational sites.

In 2024, we made the strategic decision to close sites in Australia, Canada, Portugal, and the Netherlands as part of efforts to optimize our global asset footprint and adapt our manufacturing lines to evolving market conditions.

claims.claim_text: Indorama Ventures conducts biennial materiality assessments, complemented by annual reviews, to identify and prioritize the ESG topics most relevant to our business and stakeholders.

In 2024, the assessment was conducted in alignment with the EU CSRD and the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS), and further aligned with key frameworks such as the GRI Standards 2021, IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, and DJSI.
External verification is a critical component in enhancing the credibility and transparency of our disclosures.

claims.claim_text: To ensure compliance with the GRI Standards 2021, IIRC Integrated Reporting (<IR>), and the AA1000 Assurance Standard v3, we engaged TÜV India Private Limited as our independent external auditor.

claims.claim_text: TÜV NORD CERT GmbH conducted third-party verification of our Scope 1, 2, and 3 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across nine categories, in accordance with the GHG Protocol, ISO 14064-1, and ISO 14064-3.
claims.section: Sustainability Report Assurance and GHG Verification

claims.claim_text: We follow the Greenhouse Gas Protocol on Corporate Accounting and Reporting, developed by the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD).
The Report is developed based on GRI Standards 2021, IIRC Integrated Reporting (<IR>), and AA1000 Assurance Standard V.3 (Type 1, Moderate Level).

Indorama Ventures has developed the Report content and is responsible for the identification of materiality through the double materiality assessment, corresponding ESG issues, identifying, establishing, and reporting performance management, data management, and quality.

Indorama Ventures' management team takes responsibility for the accurate preparation of the Report in reference to the applied criteria of GRI Standards 2021 and IIRC Integrated Reporting (<IR>) framework.
The assurance engagement encompasses a review of the evidence (on a sample basis) for identified ESG indicators.
Verification of the reliability of the GRI Standards disclosure on environmental and social topics.
The reporting boundary for the above topics cover 150 operating sites across 33 countries in 2024.

The Report was evaluated against the following criteria: adherence to the principles of stakeholder inclusiveness, materiality, responsiveness, completeness, neutrality, relevance, sustainability context, accuracy, reliability, comparability, clarity, and timeliness, as prescribed in the GRI Standards 2021, IIRC Integrated Reporting (<IR>), and AA1000 Assurance Standard V.3 along with AA1000 AccountAbility Principles (2018).
The training hours per year per employee can be increased by setting appropriate target
The safety checklist and vendor evaluation attributes 10 % weightage for safety parameters, revisiting the same is requested
Indorama Ventures can evaluate the impact of the introduction of green hydrogen to reduce its scope-1 emissions
Where possible, Indorama Ventures can make provision for the dedicated monitoring of CoD, rather than modelling CoD values
Indorama Ventures appropriately discloses the KPIs and actions that focus on the creation of value over the short, medium, and long term.
TUVI is of the opinion that the reported disclosures generally meet the GRI Standards 2021 reporting requirements.
Indorama Ventures followed GRI 1 Foundation 2021: Requirements and Principles for using the GRI Standards; GRI 2: General Disclosures 2021: Disclosures about the reporting organization.

TÜV Nord Cert GmbH has verified the information on GHG Scope 1 and 2 emissions in reference to the GHG Protocol, ISO 14064-1, and ISO 14064-3 to ascertain the GHG reporting process in line with standards.
TUVI confirms that Indorama Ventures has transparently reported major material information pertaining to all its six capitals in line with the <IR> framework.
Stakeholder identification and engagement is carried out by Indorama Ventures on a periodic basis to bring out key stakeholder concerns as material topics of significant stakeholders.
Indorama Ventures established the relationship between ESG and organizational strategy within the Report, as well as the context in which disclosures are made.
The materiality determination process has been conducted and reviewed based on the principle of double materiality and the requirements of the GRI Standards.
The respective Carbon Footprint was verified by TÜV NORD CERT GmbH in accordance with DIN EN ISO 14064-3: 2020 regarding its correctness and completeness for Indorama Ventures Public Company Ltd.

Acting as an independent Certification Body TÜV NORD CERT GmbH has verified the carbon footprint of the organization for the reporting period 01.01.2024 - 31.12.2024 to be 43,677,023 t CO₂e (details s. annex).
The level of assurance is reasonable.
The carbon footprint includes Scopes 1 and 2 (location-based approach).

This report was prepared in adherence with the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) standards core option and the International Integrated Reporting Council (IIRC)’s International Integrated Reporting Framework 2021.
